title: Quotient interpretations of first-order theories
summary: Interpret first-order objects by definable equivalence classes of tuples, preserving native truth through representative choices and guarded quantifiers.
abstract: Different descriptions may represent the same mathematical object. A quotient interpretation makes this precise by selecting tuples in an existing structure and identifying them through a definable equivalence relation. Functions need one output class, although several output tuples may represent it. We prove that the defining relations and operations descend to classes, then translate logical equality through the equivalence relation and retain every quantified coordinate block. The resulting native first-order translation preserves truth and transfers theories and their consequences. An example discarding a redundant coordinate shows why unique representatives would impose an unnecessary restriction.
